turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. Room two's free. On the repeat list sumatriptan is down as one hundred milligrams, when required.
[SEG0002] person_2 (CAREGIVER): That's not what he takes. The box at home is fifty milligrams.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): I'll flag it. Pressure just now was one hundred and thirty-six over eighty-four, pulse seventy-two.
[SEG0007] person_4 (DOCTOR): Same as your usual ones?
[SEG0011] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Much worse when he wakes, most mornings for the last three weeks. The ordinary headaches have been about eight years, give or take.
[SEG0013] person_2 (CAREGIVER): He gets up and he's—
[SEG0018] person_2 (CAREGIVER): More like two or three times a—
[SEG0024] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Two five-hundred milligram tablets, every day, for the head.
[SEG0027] person_1 (NURSE): Sorry to butt in. The label really does print one hundred, from the last issue—
[SEG0028] person_2 (CAREGIVER): He's never had the hundred. It's Imigran fifty, swallowed, two or three times a week, for the migraines.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right. The old diagnosis is migraine?
[SEG0031] person_2 (CAREGIVER): He snores as well, every night, really loud, and he's—
[SEG0035] person_2 (CAREGIVER): He does. And he's tired all day, nods off in the armchair after tea.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): So no daytime tiredness, from your point of view.
[SEG0040] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Oh, the car park ticket runs out at half—
[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): Shoes can stay on. Up on the couch and follow my finger.
[SEG0049] person_4 (DOCTOR): Pupils equal and reacting, no facial droop, grip strong in both hands.
[SEG0050] person_4 (DOCTOR): Power full in the arms and legs, reflexes brisk and equal, heel-to-toe steady.
[SEG0051] person_4 (DOCTOR): I think the migraine pattern may be shifting, but with the morning headache and vomiting I can't exclude a pressure problem.
[SEG0052] person_2 (CAREGIVER): So does he need a scan?
[SEG0053] person_4 (DOCTOR): If you're still being sick most mornings when I see you in two weeks, I'll arrange a CT head. Not before.
[SEG0054] person_4 (DOCTOR): Come back and see me in two weeks regardless. If the headache goes sudden and severe, or you can't wake him, go straight to A&E.
[SEG0056] person_2 (CAREGIVER): I'll get him there. We were late today because the ring road was—
[SEG0058] person_1 (NURSE): I'll book the two-week slot at the desk on your way out.

spec.situation: Person with long headaches who now has a different pattern (worse in the morning, or with vomiting); takes sumatriptan or paracetamol often; partner says snoring and tiredness too; patient dismisses it. Doctor does a quick neuro exam and orders a scan conditionally.
features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.

bad.reason: Duration/frequency conflated: 8 years applies ordinary headaches; most mornings/3 weeks applies worse waking headaches.
bad.text: headaches (category=neurological, status=present, duration=approximately 8 years, frequency=most mornings, onset=worsening over the last 3 weeks, temporality=current, reported_by=caregiver, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Sumatriptan current dose is 50 mg orally; the medication entry is missing the dose.
Patient denied taking sumatriptan every day; use is two to three times a week rather than daily.
Patient/caregiver said there are no other tablets being taken.
Patient denied daytime tiredness; doctor documented no daytime tiredness from the patient's point of view. This denial/conflict is not captured as a negative finding.

omissions.text: Sumatriptan dose reported as 50 mg orally (Imigran 50); the current medication entry is missing the dose despite the transcript specifying it repeatedly.

The patient denied being sick with the headaches every day; vomiting was reported as having occurred twice this week rather than most mornings. This matters because the plan for CT was contingent on still being sick most mornings at review.
